messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Debugging tips? Error 9
parts:
that is way beyond what inla is supposed to handle, and why inla stop when you have more than 38 thetas (which is the current upper limit in the table of designs used for the ccd integration). 

do you really need all the the thetas?  can you group them, saying some of the rw1 has the same precision (you do this using the option 'replicate' see 

http://www.r-inla.org/models/tools

alternative, is also to turn off the numerical integration of the hyperparameters, using

inla(..., control.inla = list(int.strategy = "eb"))

H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Debugging tips? Error 9
parts:
I'm trying to use the rw1 models as non-parametric random effects. I used your earlier advice to fill in NAs to make it so that each random effect only applied to a subset of the data, but maybe I misinterpreted. Here's the type of model I want:

y ~ BX + f_region(year, rw1) + f_region(age, rw1)

Right now I've got separate random effects for each of the 21 regions, with the year and age vectors parsed out into 21 separate indicators. Since I do in fact want the same hyperparameters for each, I'll try the replicant approach. Thanks again.

> I'm trying to use the rw1 models as non-parametric random effects. I
> used your earlier advice to fill in NAs to make it so that each random
> effect only applied to a subset of the data, but maybe I
> misinterpreted. Here's the type of model I want:
>
>
> y ~ BX + f_region(year, rw1) + f_region(age, rw1)
>
>
> Right now I've got separate random effects for each of the 21 regions,
> with the year and age vectors parsed out into 21 separate indicators.
> Since I do in fact want the same hyperparameters for each, I'll try
> the replicant approach. Thanks again.

I think you may want the random effects in each of the 21 regions to
have the same precision, which you can write as

f(year, model ="rw1", replicate = region)

where region \in 1.... nregion.

this extention is explained in

http://www.r-inla.org/models/tools


same for age.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Debugging tips? Error 9
parts: Thanks Havard, after rereading the docs on replication I picked that up and it gave me the desired results. My problem was reading c(y1,y2,y3) as cbind(y1,y2,y3) when first going through the docs, so I mistakenly thought that replicate was used when there were multiple outcomes per observation. I didn't notice replicate or copy used in any of the Volume I or II examples, so could I suggest that an example of each would be helpful? Now that I've seen a use case I understand that they're extraordinarily useful.
